cases.question: A customer paid USD 1,200 for an invoice dated 24 September 2026, captured at 11:00 IST that day. What is that in INR at the official reference rate, and when will it settle for a Mumbai merchant?
cases.answer:
USD 1,200 comes to INR 1,15,091.88 at the official reference rate. The payment should settle around Monday, 28 September 2026 for a Mumbai merchant.

The rate:
- The rate used is the FBIL reference rate for 24 September 2026, the invoice date: INR 95.9099 per USD.
- This is a reference rate. It is not necessarily the rate your bank or payment gateway actually applied.

The settlement date (T+2 working days, Mumbai):
- The payment was captured on Thursday, 24 September at 11:00 IST.
- Working day 1 is Friday, 25 September.
- Saturday, 26 September is skipped because it is the 4th Saturday.
- Sunday, 27 September is skipped because it is a Sunday.
- Working day 2 is Monday, 28 September, the estimated settlement date.

This date is only an estimate, based on RBI's Mumbai holiday list and Razorpay's published T+2 rule. It is not the provider's actual settlement schedule, and it doesn't account for cut-off times, payment-method rules or holds.

The data source flagged the FBIL rate data as out of date, because it only goes up to 24 September. That doesn't affect this answer, since the 24 September rate itself has been published.

cases.answer:

The payment was captured on Friday, 27 March 2026, which counts as T. Only bank working days count towards T+2 for the Mumbai office:
- Working day 1: Monday, 30 March 2026
- Working day 2: Thursday, 2 April 2026, the estimated settlement date

- 29 March 2026: Sunday

This date is based on the RBI holiday list for Mumbai and the T+2 working-day rule. It isn't the payment provider's own schedule, and it doesn't cover cut-off times, rules for particular payment methods, or holds on the payment.

cases.question: What is the USD/INR reference rate for 14 September 2026? If there is no rate for that exact day, tell me which day's rate applies and why.
cases.answer:
No rate was published for 14 September 2026, so the rate from 11 September 2026 applies: 1 USD = 95.7245 INR. This is the FBIL reference rate.

Why 11 September:
- 14 September 2026 (Monday) was a bank holiday for Ganesh Chaturthi / Vinayakar Chathurthi, so FBIL didn't publish a rate.
- The days before it were the weekend (12 September, Saturday, and 13 September, Sunday). Neither day had a published rate either.
- The latest published rate before 14 September is from Friday, 11 September 2026, so that's the one in force.

Note: The FX data source is a bit behind. Its latest rate is from 24 September, not today. That doesn't affect this answer, because the 11 September rate was published well before then.

This is a reference rate. It isn't the rate your bank, card network or payment gateway actually used.

cases.question: What was the FBIL MIBOR on Friday 4 September 2026, and what tenor does that figure cover?
cases.answer:
FBIL MIBOR for Friday 4 September 2026 was 4.91% per annum. The tenor is 3D, which runs over the weekend from Friday to Monday 7 September. It is not a standard one-night overnight rate.

- On Fridays, FBIL publishes a 3D rate in place of the usual one-night (O/N) rate, because money lent on Friday is repaid on Monday.
- FBIL published this figure on 4 September 2026 at 12:45 IST.
- FBIL's MIBOR data here only runs up to 24 September 2026, so it is behind (data up to 30 September should exist by now). This doesn't affect the 4 September figure, but rates after 24 September aren't available yet.

cases.question: List the bank holidays in Mumbai in April 2026.
cases.answer:
RBI lists 3 bank holidays for Mumbai in April 2026:

1. Wednesday 1 April: Banks close their yearly accounts. This is an account-closing holiday. Banks are closed to the public, but it is not a full NI Act holiday.
2. Friday 3 April: Good Friday (NI Act holiday, banks closed).
3. Tuesday 14 April: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Jayanti (NI Act holiday). RBI lists this date under several regional festival names: Maha Vishuva Sankranti, Biju, Buisu, Tamil New Year's Day, Bohag Bihu, Cheiraoba and Baisakhi.

Sundays and the 2nd and 4th Saturdays are also non-working days, but RBI doesn't list them. In April 2026 those are Sundays 5, 12, 19 and 26 April, and Saturdays 11 April (2nd) and 25 April (4th).

Source: RBI holiday list, last fetched 25 September 2026 and marked as current.
